title: Salvianolic acid a inhibits neuroinflammation and ameliorates Alzheimer's disease pathology via the p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway based on network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Xiao, Shifeng; Han, Yuping; Yan, Ji; Wu, Lijuan; Lin, Haitong; Yuan, Cuiyi; Song, Changjie; Ye, Jinwang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹酚酸A通过p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB通路抑制神经炎症改善阿尔茨海默病，仅涉及药物-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作、TF-DNA结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) represents the most prevalent form of neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by progressive cognitive impairments and a scarcity of effective treatments. Salvianolic acid A (SalA), a natural phytochemical endowed with antioxidative, antiapoptotic, and anti-inflammatory properties, emerges as a promising therapeutic candidate for AD. This study explored the therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of SalA in mitigating AD-related pathologies. Through integrative network pharmacology, molecular docking, and pathway enrichment analysis, p38 MAPK and NF-kappaB were identified as potential targets of SalA in the context of AD. SalA treatment inhibited the activation of the p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway via targeting p38 MAPK, leading to decreased levels of IL-1alpha and IL-1beta in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated HMC3 cells. In an in vivo 3 x Tg-AD mouse model, SalA administration ameliorated cognitive decline associated with AD, decreased tau protein hyperphosphorylation in the hippocampus and cortex, and reduced amyloid-beta (Abeta) accumulation and beta-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) levels. Furthermore, SalA attenuated the activation of the p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway and the expression of related inflammatory cytokines in the brains of 3 x Tg-AD mice. In conclusion, this study elucidates the promising ameliorative effects of SalA on improving AD pathology, primarily through the modulation of the p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是最常见的神经退行性疾病形式，其特征为进行性认知障碍及有效治疗手段的匮乏。丹酚酸A（Salvianolic acid A, SalA）作为一种天然植物化学物，具有抗氧化、抗凋亡和抗炎特性，成为治疗AD的有前景候选药物。本研究探讨了SalA在缓解AD相关病理中的治疗功效及其潜在机制。通过整合网络药理学、分子对接和通路富集分析，p38 MAPK和NF-kappaB被确定为SalA在AD背景下的潜在靶点。SalA处理通过靶向p38 MAPK抑制了p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB通路的激活，导致脂多糖（lipopolysaccharide, LPS）刺激的HMC3细胞中IL-1alpha和IL-1beta水平降低。在体内3 x Tg-AD小鼠模型中，SalA给药改善了与AD相关的认知衰退，降低了海马和皮层中tau蛋白过度磷酸化，并减少了淀粉样蛋白-beta（amyloid-beta, Abeta）积累及β-位点淀粉样前体蛋白裂解酶1（beta-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1, BACE1）水平。此外，SalA减弱了3 x Tg-AD小鼠大脑中p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB通路的激活及相关炎症因子的表达。总之，本研究阐明了SalA主要通过调节p38 MAPK/NF-kappaB信号通路，在改善AD病理方面具有前景的缓解作用。
